comments.story: The Rise and Fall of Silicon Graphics
comments.why: Video on the SGI Indigo2 workstation.
comments.text: Random trivia which will likely get buried but whatever: the rendering software Octane Render got its name from my refusing to let the author use my rendering software's name, and he had some historical beef with us, the two devs of Indigo Renderer, so he named his renderer after the SGI machine that came after the Indigo, Octane. He also leant his SGI Indigo2 to the LGR guy on YouTube, and he did a great video on it: [VIDEO]

comments.author: ckozlowski
comments.story: A baby saved ‘Toy Story 2’ from near complete deletion (2021)
comments.why: Covers SGI workstations like the Octane.
comments.text: You're on the right track. As told in the Next Web story, the workstation in question was a Silicon Graphics Octane or there abouts. These were incredibly expensive and were provided by the company. In addition, according to the story, they were the ones who set up the file sync for her to be able to work from home. LGR and RMC have both done videos on the SGI Octane and are worth watching: [VIDEO] , [LINK] Edit: It was Retro Man Cave, not Adrian's Digital Basement as originally written.

comments.author: w_s_l
comments.story: The charm of buying old workstation hardware on the cheap
comments.why: SGI workstation as object of nostalgia.
comments.text: For one I would love to have an SGI workstation, I still have CG magazines from this era and its plastered everywhere in the ads, and I'm still amazed at the graphic output (so smooth) and what we had in the 90s. [VIDEO] I'd imagine something like this would've been used to make Crash Bandicoot and likes. It'd be really interesting to play games built on this thing.
